verses.sanskrit:
जनमेजय उवाच।
              
              प्राप्य राज्यं महाबाहुर्धर्मपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः । यदन्यदकरोद्विप्र तन्मे वक्तुमिहार्हसि ॥१॥
verses.english: By acting how, O you who are conversant with all courses of conduct, did Janaka the king of Mithila, versed in the religion of Liberation, succeed in acquiring Liberation, after casting off all worldly enjoyments?

verses.sanskrit: भगवान्वा हृषीकेशस्त्रैलोक्यस्य परो गुरुः । ऋषे यदकरोद्वीरस्तच्च व्याख्यातुमर्हसि ॥२॥
verses.english: “Regarding it is cited the following old narrative of the particular conduct by which that king, a master of all courses of conduct, succeeded in acquiring the highest happiness.

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              शृणु तत्त्वेन राजेन्द्र कीर्त्यमानं मयाऽनघ । वासुदेवं पुरस्कृत्य यदकुर्वत पाण्डवाः ॥३॥
verses.english: There was a king in Mithila of the name of Janadeva of Janaka's race. He was ever engaged in thinking of the courses of conduct that might lead to the attainment of Brahma.

verses.sanskrit: प्राप्य राज्यं महाराज कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः । चातुर्वर्ण्यं यथायोग्यं स्वे स्वे स्थाने न्यवेशयत् ॥४॥
verses.english: One hundred preceptors always used to live in his palace, describing to him the various courses of duty followed by people who had adopted the various modes of life.

verses.sanskrit: ब्राह्मणानां सहस्रं च स्नातकानां महात्मनाम् । सहस्रं निष्कमेकैकं दापयामास पाण्डवः ॥५॥
verses.english: Well read in the Vedas, he was not very well satisfied with the speculations of his instructors on the nature of the Soul, and in their teachings of his extinction upon the dissolution of the body or of re-birth after death.

verses.sanskrit: तथाऽनुजीविनो भृत्यान्संश्रितानतिथीनपि । कामैः सन्तर्पयामास कृपणांस्तर्ककानपि ॥६॥
verses.english: Once upon a time a great ascetic named Panchashikha the son of Kapila, having roamed over the whole world, arrived at Mithila.

verses.sanskrit: पुरोहिताय धौम्याय प्रादादयुतशः स गाः । धनं सुवर्णं रजतं वासांसि विविधान्यपि ॥७॥
verses.english: Having made conclusions about the diverse duties connected with renunciation, he was above all pairs of opposites, and had no doubts.

verses.sanskrit: कृपाय च महाराज गुरुवृत्तिमवर्तत । विदुराय च राजाऽसौ पूजां चक्रे यतव्रतः ॥८॥
verses.english: He was considered as the foremost of Rishis. Living wherever he pleased, he wished to place before the reach of all men eternal happiness that is so difficult of attainment.

verses.sanskrit: भक्ष्यान्नपानैर्विविधसैर्वासोभिः शयनासनैः । सर्वान्सन्तोषयामास संश्रितान्ददतां वरः ॥९॥
verses.english: It appeared that he roamed, amazing the world, having put on the form of none else then that great Rishi, that lord of creatures, whom the followers of the Sankhya doctrine knew by the name of Kapila.

verses.sanskrit: लब्धप्रशमनं कृत्वा स राजा राजसत्तम । युयुत्सोर्धार्तराष्ट्रस्य पूजां चक्रे महायशाः ॥१०॥
verses.english: He was the greatest of all the disciples of Asuri and was called the undying. He had performed a mental Sacrifice lasting for a thousand years.

verses.sanskrit: धृतराष्ट्राय तद्राज्यं गान्धार्यै विदुराय च । निवेद्य सुस्थवद्राजा सुखमास्ते युधिष्ठिरः ॥११॥
verses.english: He was firm in mind, and had performed all the rites and sacrifices that are enjoyed in the scriptures and that lead to the attainment of Brahma. He knew full well the five sacs that cover the Soul. He was devoted to the five acts regarding the adoration of Brahma, and had the five qualities. Know by the name of Panchashikha, he had approached one day a large assembly of Rishis following the Sankhya doctrines and enquired of them about the highest object of human acquisition, namely, the Unmanifest or that upon which the five sacs rest.
verses.bhavadeepa: लब्धप्रशमनं लब्धस्य धनादेः यथोचितमंशतः पात्रे समर्पणेन शान्तिकम् ॥१०॥

verses.sanskrit: तथा सर्वं स नगरं प्रसाद्य भरतर्षभ । वासुदेवं महात्मानमभ्यगच्छत्कृताञ्जलिः ॥१२॥
verses.english: For acquiring a knowledge of the Soul, Asuri had enquired of his preceptor. On account of the latter's instructions and of his own penances, Asuri understood the distinction between the body and the Soul and had gained celestial vision.

verses.sanskrit: ततो महति पर्यङ्के मणिकाञ्चनभूषिते । ददर्श कृष्णमासीनं नीलमेघसमद्युतिम् ॥१३॥
verses.english: In that assembly of ascetics, Asuri described the Immutable, One, and Indestructible Brahma which is seen in various forms.

verses.sanskrit: जाज्वल्यमानं वपुषा दिव्याभरणभूषितम् । पीतकौशेयवसनं हेम्नेवोपगतं मणिम् ॥१४॥
verses.english: Panchashikha became a disciple of Asuri. He lived on human milk. There was a certain Brahman lady named Kapila. She was Asuri's wife.

verses.sanskrit: कौस्तुभेनोरसिस्थेन मणिनाऽभिविराजितम् । उद्यतेवोदयं शैलं सूर्येणाभिविराजितम् ॥१५॥
verses.english: Panchashikha was accepted by her as a son and he used to suck her breasts. For this, he came to be known as the son of Kapila and his understanding became fixed on Brahma.

verses.sanskrit: नौपम्यं विद्यते तस्य त्रिषु लोकेषु किंचन । सोऽभिगम्य महात्मानं विष्णुं पुरुषविग्रहम् ॥१६॥
verses.english: The divine Rishi said to me, all this, regarding the circumstances of his birth and those about his becoming the son of Kapila. The latter also told me about the omniscience of Panchashikha.

verses.sanskrit: उवाच मधुरं राजा स्मितपूर्वमिदं तदा । सुखेन ते निशा कच्चिद्व्युष्टा बुद्धिमतां वर ॥१७॥
कच्चिज्ज्ञानानि सर्वाणि प्रसन्नानि तवाच्युत । तथैवोपश्रिता देवी बुद्धिर्बुद्धिमतां वर ॥१८॥
verses.english: Knowing fully all the forms of duty, Panchashikha, after having himself gained high knowledge, (came to Janaka) and knowing that that king had equal reverence for all his preceptors, began to startle those hundred preceptors (by a very sensible exposition of his doctrine).

verses.sanskrit: वयं राज्यमनुप्राप्ताः पृथिवी च वशे स्थिता । तव प्रसादाद्भगवंस्त्रिलोकगतिविक्रम ॥१९॥
verses.english: Marking the genius of the son of Kapila, Janaka became exceedingly attacked to him, and abandoning his hundred preceptors, began to follow him.

verses.sanskrit: जयं प्राप्ता यशश्चाग्र्यं न च धर्मच्युता वयम् । तं तथा भाषमाणं तु धर्मराजमरिन्दमम् । नोवाच भगवान्किञ्चिद्ध्यानमेवान्वपद्यत ॥२०॥
verses.english: Then Kapila's son began to discourse to Janaka, who had according to the ordinance bent his head to him and who was fully competent to understand the sage's instructions, upon that great religion of Liberation which is explained in Sankhya treatises.
